newsitem.title: GERMANY: Oil World sees lower linseed output in 1996/97.
newsitem.headline: Oil World sees lower linseed output in 1996/97.

text.p: World output of linseed will decline by 12 percent in 1996/97 to 2.29 million tonnes, the independent publication Oil World newsletter said.

The global linseed area was cut to 3.54 million hectares from 3.89 million last year as farmers preferred to plant lucrative grains for the 1996 harvest, namely in Canada, which accounts for 95 percent of all exports, the U.S. and Argentina.
Canadian yields were above expectations but its 1996 crop of 850,000 tonnes would be well below last year's 1.10 million so that domestic stocks needed to be cut.
World crushings were seen steady in 96/97 at 1.98 million tonnes, with sharply lower activity in Argentina but higher levels in Europe and Canada.

Lin oil prices should be boosted by a decline in output amid an overall favourable demand outlook for oils and fats. Oil World put oil output in Oct/Sept 96/97 at 660,000 tonnes (673,000 95/96) and consumption at 677,000 (675,000).
Lin meal output in 96/97 was seen at 1.26 million tonnes (1.28 million 95/96) and use at 1.28 million (1.30 million previously).
